question: Should OpenClaw accept static `sandbox.docker.env` SecretRefs when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but the permanent security/product boundary is whether SecretRef-backed credentials should be allowed on an env surface that already has documented Docker metadata exposure.

options.title: Accept with explicit boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR only after maintainer/security review records that this exposure is acceptable with aligned docs, audit, and configure behavior.

options.title: Require stronger warnings first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to explicitly name SecretRef-backed Docker env exposure in user docs before landing the otherwise narrow implementation.

options.title: Reject env-based delivery
options.body: Pause or close the linked PR and design a non-env secret delivery mechanism if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept with explicit boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR only after maintainer/security review records that this exposure is acceptable with aligned docs, audit, and configure behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored both the adjacent Docker env propagation fix and the related SecretRef runtime work, making him the strongest technical routing candidate for this boundary decision.
